html:
Alexander the Great was king of Macedon from 336 BCE until his death in 323 BCE, aged 32. In about eleven years he conquered the Persian Empire and led his army from Greece to Egypt and into northwest India.

He was the son of Philip II and Olympias, and was taught as a teenager by Aristotle. At eighteen he led the cavalry at the Battle of Chaeronea. When Philip was murdered he took the throne, crushed revolts and destroyed Thebes as a warning.

His campaign, the conquests of Alexander, began in 334 BCE:

  • He beat the Persians at the Granicus in 334 BCE, at Issus in 333 BCE and at Gaugamela in 331 BCE.
  • He took Egypt and founded Alexandria.
  • He burned Persepolis, then fought for years in Bactria and Sogdia.
  • He crossed into India and beat King Porus at the Hydaspes in 326 BCE, but his army refused to go further.

He died in Babylon, probably of illness. His generals split the empire into kingdoms such as Seleucid Asia and Ptolemaic Egypt, and Greek language and culture spread across the Middle East for centuries.
sum: Alexander the Great was king of Macedon from 336 BCE until his death in 323 BCE, aged 32. In about eleven years he conquered the Persian Empire and led his army from Greece to Egypt and into northwest India.
